I've saved the Q3 results to `answer.json`. Run the same way on Q2, the script reproduces all 10 reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with highest net sales | enterprise, 328,213,993 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 244 |
| c. Category with highest net sales | svc, 340,751,713 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with largest refund total | u176@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 226 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 685,292 |
| h. September vs. August growth | -8.7% |

The Q2 check only matched once I handled three things in the data:
- **Time zone:** Order times are stored in UTC. I converted them to Korea time (UTC+9) before assigning quarters and months.
- **Segment labels:** The same segment appears in different forms, e.g. `Enterprise ` and `enterprise`. I trimmed spaces and lowercased them before grouping.
- **Duplicate customers:** There are 300 customer IDs but only 250 distinct emails. I counted customers by email (trimmed, lowercased), which affects b, e and f.

STATUS: DONE
